result.journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making
result.keywords:
Abstract
Background
Deep learning methods have shown strong performance in named entity recognition for Chinese clinical records, but heterogeneous document structure and overlapping medical expressions remain challenging. In particular, combining token-level context with modality-aware attention can improve the extraction of diagnoses, symptoms, and treatments from electronic medical records.

Methods
We propose a self-attention guided deep network that integrates part-of-speech features and multimodal clinical context. The model uses a dual-path encoder to capture character and word representations, followed by an adaptive attention fusion module to emphasize clinically informative spans across structured notes and narrative text. A conditional decoding layer is applied to generate entity labels for medical named entity recognition.

Results
Experiments on a Chinese electronic medical record corpus show improved precision, recall, and F1 score over baseline BiLSTM-CRF and attention-only systems. The model performs particularly well on disease and examination entities while maintaining stable results across longer discharge summaries.

Conclusions
The proposed method demonstrates that self-attention and modality-aware fusion can enhance named entity recognition in Chinese medical text, supporting downstream information extraction in clinical decision support systems.
